Week in brief

Sentinel SAP connector retirement sets a September 14 migration deadline

The clearest operational deadline is Sentinel’s permanent retirement of the containerized SAP connector agent on September 14, 2026. Defender XDR will also change Purview DLP alert handling on October 12, while Defender for Office 365 is rolling out email prompt-injection protection through October. Separate guidance materially clarifies Linux antivirus enforcement and preview sensor activation for non-domain-controller identity servers.

  • Sentinel · Developer and API
    Sentinel will disable the containerized SAP connector on September 14

    Microsoft says the containerized SAP connector agent will be permanently retired and disabled on September 14, 2026. New deployments should use the agentless connector, and existing deployments should migrate before SAP logs stop; existing analytics rules, workbooks, and playbooks remain functional with the agentless path.

  • Defender XDR · General
    Defender XDR will default Purview DLP alerts to behaviors October 12

    Starting October 12, 2026, Microsoft Defender XDR will treat Microsoft Purview DLP alerts as behaviors by default, reducing alert volume while keeping DLP data available in Advanced Hunting and Purview. Administrators can disable the rule to retain those alerts in the Defender XDR incident queue.

  • Defender XDR · Email and collaboration
    Defender for Office 365 rolls out email prompt-injection protection

    The protection detects and quarantines malicious email content aimed at AI assistants. It applies to organizations with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft 365 E5, with automatic high-confidence threat quarantine enabled by default as rollout continues through October 2026.

  • Endpoint · Endpoint protection
    Linux guidance specifies four Defender antivirus enforcement levels

    The updated Defender for Endpoint on Linux guidance documents four enforcement levels, identifies passive mode as the default, and adds audit mode as a preview capability. Audit mode requires Defender for Endpoint version 101.26062.0007 or later, and the article adds a command for checking the active enforcement level.

  • Identity · Architecture and deployment
    Defender for Identity v3.x covers preview activation on non-domain controllers

    Version 3.x sensor guidance now includes eligible AD FS, AD CS, and Microsoft Entra Connect servers that are not domain controllers. Activation on those servers is in preview, requires manual activation, and does not support automatic activation or migration; deployments limited to those servers also need at least one v3.x sensor on a domain controller.

For Defender administrators

Administrators running the containerized SAP connector should migrate to the agentless connector before September 14 and use the agentless option for new systems. Defender XDR teams should decide whether to keep the new DLP behavior default or disable it to preserve DLP alerts in the Defender XDR incident queue. Linux administrators should check the Defender version requirement before using audit mode, and identity teams deploying sensors only on non-domain-controller servers must install at least one v3.x sensor on a domain controller and use manual activation.

This period briefing was generated by AI from the tracked Microsoft Learn and Message Center changes.
